CHIEF COMPLAINT
Right elbow pain

HISTORY OF PRESENT ILLNESS
Patient is a 40-50 year old male presenting with right elbow pain that began approximately one week ago while playing lacrosse with his children (ages 13 and 10). He reports the pain started when throwing a ball during play. He states his 13-year-old child was checking him with a lacrosse stick multiple times, and he may have been struck in the elbow during this contact. He denies a fall. The pain is described as sharp, localized to the tip of the elbow, and worsened with movement. The pain radiates down the forearm. He has taken ibuprofen (Advil) for a couple of days with some relief. Denies chest pain or abdominal pain.

REVIEW OF SYSTEMS
Denies chest pain. Denies abdominal pain. Lungs clear bilaterally. Heart regular.

PAST MEDICAL HISTORY
Hypertension
Type 2 diabetes mellitus
Grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur (known, stable)

MEDICATIONS
Lisinopril 20 mg daily
Metformin 500 mg daily

ALLERGIES
Not documented

FAMILY HISTORY
Not documented

SOCIAL HISTORY
Plays lacrosse with his children. Follows Mediterranean diet with low salt intake. Reports compliance with dietary modifications since pandemic.

PHYSICAL EXAMINATION
Blood pressure: 150/90 mmHg (elevated)
Cardiovascular: Regular rate and rhythm, grade 2/6 systolic ejection murmur noted
Lungs: Clear to auscultation bilaterally
Right elbow: Swelling and bruising noted. Tenderness to palpation over olecranon. Mild pain with flexion and extension. Normal range of motion maintained.

RESULTS
Right elbow X-ray: Normal, no fracture, no bony abnormality
Fasting blood glucose: 80-100 mg/dL (patient reports values in this range when checked)

ASSESSMENT AND PLAN
1. Right elbow contusion secondary to blunt trauma from lacrosse stick. Ibuprofen 800 mg twice daily for pain and inflammation. Ice application 3 times daily for 20 minutes per session. Restrict lacrosse activity for next 2 weeks to allow healing.
2. Hypertension. Continue lisinopril 20 mg daily. Elevated BP today may be related to white coat syndrome. Continue Mediterranean diet with low salt intake. Patient reports good compliance.
3. Type 2 diabetes mellitus. Continue metformin 500 mg daily. Order A1C to assess glycemic control and determine if dose adjustment is needed.
4. Follow-up as needed. Nurse will provide prescriptions prior to discharge.
